data must reference rows * rowstride bytes
palette must point to at least palsize entries
On success, caller must destroy with ncvisual_destroy()

functions.name: ncvisual_from_plane
functions.signature: struct ncvisual* ncvisual_from_plane(const struct ncplane* n, ncblitter_e blit, int begy, int begx, unsigned leny, unsigned lenx)
functions.description: Promote an ncplane’s graphics (spaces/half-blocks/full-blocks) to an ncvisual for further transformations.
requirements: n must not be NULL
Plane may contain only spaces, half blocks, and full blocks; other glyphs cause failure
Lengths of 0 mean “all remaining area” from the origin begy/begx
On success, caller must destroy ncvisual with ncvisual_destroy()

functions.name: ncvisual_from_sixel
functions.signature: struct ncvisual* ncvisual_from_sixel(const char* s, unsigned leny, unsigned lenx)
functions.description: Create an ncvisual from a NUL-terminated Sixel control sequence string, with expected pixel geometry.
requirements: s must be a valid, NUL-terminated Sixel sequence
leny and lenx specify size metadata for the decoded image
On success, caller must destroy with ncvisual_destroy()

functions.name: ncvisual_geom
functions.signature: int ncvisual_geom(const struct notcurses* nc, const struct ncvisual* n, const struct ncvisual_options* vopts, ncvgeom* geom)
functions.description: Compute visual, cell, and rendering geometries for an ncvisual given environment and options. Fills out ncvgeom.
requirements: geom must not be NULL
At least one of nc or n must be non-NULL (otherwise only certain fields can be computed as documented)
If only nc is provided, only terminal/cell-related fields are filled; if only n is provided, only pixy/pixx are filled

functions.name: ncvisual_destroy
functions.signature: void ncvisual_destroy(struct ncvisual* ncv)
functions.description: Destroy/free an ncvisual. Rendered content already on planes is not affected.
requirements: ncv may be NULL (safe to call if unknown)
Must be called exactly once per successful creation to avoid leaks

functions.name: ncvisual_decode
functions.signature: int ncvisual_decode(struct ncvisual* nc)
functions.description: Decode the next frame from the visual. Returns 0 on success, 1 on end-of-file, -1 on failure.
requirements: nc must be a valid ncvisual created from decodable media
Subsequent calls advance frame decoding state

functions.name: ncvisual_decode_loop
functions.signature: int ncvisual_decode_loop(struct ncvisual* nc)
functions.description: Like ncvisual_decode(), but rewinds to first frame on EOF so streaming can loop. Returns same codes as decode.
requirements: nc must be a valid ncvisual
Used for looping playback; next blit will render first frame after loop

functions.name: ncvisual_rotate
functions.signature: int ncvisual_rotate(struct ncvisual* n, double rads)
functions.description: Rotate a visual in memory by ±π/2 radians (currently only ±M_PI/2 supported).
requirements: n must be valid
rads must be either M_PI/2 or -M_PI/2 (other values likely error)

functions.name: ncvisual_resize
functions.signature: int ncvisual_resize(struct ncvisual* n, int rows, int cols)
functions.description: Resize the in-memory pixel data to the specified pixel rows and columns using best available (interpolative) scaling.
requirements: n must be valid
rows > 0, cols > 0

functions.name: ncvisual_resize_noninterpolative
functions.signature: int ncvisual_resize_noninterpolative(struct ncvisual* n, int rows, int cols)
functions.description: Resize the visual using non-interpolative (naive) scaling without introducing new colors.
requirements: n must be valid
rows > 0, cols > 0

functions.name: ncvisual_polyfill_yx
functions.signature: int ncvisual_polyfill_yx(struct ncvisual* n, unsigned y, unsigned x, uint32_t rgba)
functions.description: Flood-fill at a pixel coordinate within the ncvisual with the given RGBA color. Returns count filled or -1.
requirements: n must be valid
y and x must be within the image bounds
rgba is an ABGR/byte-order RGBA value as used by ncvisuals

functions.name: ncvisual_at_yx
functions.signature: int ncvisual_at_yx(const struct ncvisual* n, unsigned y, unsigned x, uint32_t* pixel)
functions.description: Read the pixel value at (y,x) from an ncvisual into pixel.
requirements: n must be valid
y,x must be within bounds
pixel must be non-NULL

functions.name: ncvisual_set_yx
functions.signature: int ncvisual_set_yx(const struct ncvisual* n, unsigned y, unsigned x, uint32_t pixel)
functions.description: Write the given pixel value at (y,x) within an ncvisual.
requirements: n must be valid
y,x must be within bounds

functions.name: ncvisual_blit
functions.signature: struct ncplane* ncvisual_blit(struct notcurses* nc, struct ncvisual* ncv, const struct ncvisual_options* vopts)
functions.description: Render/blit the decoded visual frame to a plane based on options. May create a new plane or draw into provided one.
requirements: ncv must be valid
If NCVISUAL_OPTION_CHILDPLANE is set, vopts and vopts->n must be non-NULL
If NCVISUAL_OPTION_CHILDPLANE is not set and vopts->n is NULL, a new root plane (new pile) is created
Subregion values in vopts must be non-negative and within frame bounds
Pixels cannot be blitted to the standard plane
Returns target plane or NULL on error

functions.name: ncvisual_subtitle_plane
functions.signature: struct ncplane* ncvisual_subtitle_plane(struct ncplane* parent, const struct ncvisual* ncv)
functions.description: If a subtitle should be shown for current time/frame, returns a newly created plane (child of parent) containing it.
requirements: parent must be a valid ncplane
ncv must have subtitle data (depends on media)

functions.name: ncvisual_media_defblitter
functions.signature: ncblitter_e ncvisual_media_defblitter(const struct notcurses* nc, ncscale_e scale)
functions.description: Return the default media blitter for this environment given scale (based on UTF-8 and blitter support heuristics).
requirements: nc must be valid
scale must be a valid ncscale_e value

functions.name: ncvisual_simple_streamer
functions.signature: int ncvisual_simple_streamer(struct ncvisual* ncv, struct ncvisual_options* vopts, const struct timespec* tspec, void* curry)
functions.description: Convenience frame streamer callback: renders frames using ncvisual_blit, honoring timestamps; optionally shows subtitles via curry plane.
requirements: ncv must be valid

tspec is the target absolute time for the current frame

functions.name: ncvisual_stream
functions.signature: int ncvisual_stream(struct notcurses* nc, struct ncvisual* ncv, float timescale, ncstreamcb streamer, const struct ncvisual_options* vopts, void* curry)
functions.description: Stream all frames of a visual according to intrinsic timing scaled by timescale. Calls streamer per frame (or use simple streamer).
requirements: nc and ncv must be valid
timescale must be > 0
streamer may be NULL (then use ncvisual_simple_streamer semantics)
vopts may be NULL
Non-zero return from streamer aborts stream and is propagated

functions.name: ncblit_rgba
functions.signature: int ncblit_rgba(const void* data, int linesize, const struct ncvisual_options* vopts)
functions.description: Blit a flat RGBA buffer directly to vopts->n according to options. Returns number of pixels blitted or -1.
requirements: data must point to at least leny * linesize bytes (per vopts)
linesize is bytes per source row and must accommodate vopts->lenx*4 if fully used
vopts must be non-NULL and vopts->n must be non-NULL
beg/len fields in vopts define subregion; must be non-negative and within data bounds

functions.name: ncblit_bgrx
functions.signature: int ncblit_bgrx(const void* data, int linesize, const struct ncvisual_options* vopts)
functions.description: Blit a flat BGRx buffer (4 bytes per pixel, unused alpha) to vopts->n. Returns number of pixels or -1.
requirements: data, linesize, vopts requirements as for ncblit_rgba
vopts->n must not be NULL

functions.name: ncblit_rgb_packed
functions.signature: int ncblit_rgb_packed(const void* data, int linesize, const struct ncvisual_options* vopts, int alpha)
functions.description: Blit packed 3-byte RGB data to vopts->n applying uniform alpha to all pixels.
requirements: data must contain at least leny rows of linesize bytes
linesize must be >= vopts->lenx*3 for fully used rows
vopts and vopts->n must not be NULL
alpha typical range 0..255 (not explicitly constrained)

functions.name: ncblit_rgb_loose
functions.signature: int ncblit_rgb_loose(const void* data, int linesize, const struct ncvisual_options* vopts, int alpha)
functions.description: Blit 4-byte RGBx data to vopts->n applying uniform alpha. linesize must be a multiple of 4.
requirements: linesize must be a multiple of 4
linesize must be >= vopts->lenx*4
data valid for leny * linesize bytes
vopts and vopts->n must not be NULL
alpha typical 0..255 (not explicitly constrained)

functions.name: nctablet_userptr

functions.name: ncdirect_init
functions.signature: API ALLOC struct ncdirect* ncdirect_init(const char* termtype, FILE* fp, uint64_t flags);
functions.description: Initializes a direct-mode Notcurses context bound to the connected terminal stream fp. Direct mode lets you colorize/stylize output without full-screen rendering. termtype allows overriding terminfo type, flags is a bitmask of NCDIRECT_OPTION_* controlling behavior. Returns a heap-allocated ncdirect context on success or NULL on error (including terminfo init failure).
requirements: fp must refer to a TTY (typically stdout).
flags is a bitmask of NCDIRECT_OPTION_* constants.
If NCDIRECT_OPTION_INHIBIT_SETLOCALE is not set, the function may call setlocale() to enable UTF-8 based on LANG; be aware if your program manages locales explicitly.
On success, the returned struct ncdirect* must later be released with ncdirect_stop().

functions.name: ncdirect_core_init
functions.signature: API ALLOC struct ncdirect* ncdirect_core_init(const char* termtype, FILE* fp, uint64_t flags);
functions.description: Like ncdirect_init() but without multimedia functionality, enabling a smaller binary (link against notcurses-core). Returns a heap-allocated direct-mode context or NULL on error.
requirements: fp must refer to a TTY.
flags is a bitmask of NCDIRECT_OPTION_* constants.
Return value must be released with ncdirect_stop() on success.

functions.description: Prints the given prompt then reads a newline-delimited chunk of input from the user. Returns a heap-allocated buffer containing the input, including the newline if present, or NULL on error.
requirements: nc must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
prompt may be NULL if no prompt is desired.
Caller owns and must free the returned string on success.

Returned pointer remains valid as long as the ncdirect context is valid.

functions.name: ncdirect_hline_interp
functions.signature: API int ncdirect_hline_interp(struct ncdirect* n, const char* egc, unsigned len, uint64_t h1, uint64_t h2) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1, 2)));
functions.description: Draws a horizontal line starting at the current cursor position, repeating the single-column EGC egc for len cells, interpolating channels between h1 and h2 along the line. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
egc must be a valid UTF-8 EGC that occupies no more than one column.
len must not exceed the screen width minus the cursor’s current column offset.
Line starts at current cursor position.

functions.name: ncdirect_vline_interp
functions.signature: API int ncdirect_vline_interp(struct ncdirect* n, const char* egc, unsigned len, uint64_t h1, uint64_t h2) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1, 2)));
functions.description: Draws a vertical line starting at the current cursor position, repeating the single-column EGC egc for len rows, interpolating channels between h1 and h2 down the line. The screen will scroll as necessary. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
egc must be a valid UTF-8 EGC that occupies no more than one column.
len may be as large as desired; the screen may scroll.
Line starts at current cursor position.

functions.name: ncdirect_box
functions.signature: API int ncdirect_box(struct ncdirect* n, uint64_t ul, uint64_t ur, uint64_t ll, uint64_t lr, const wchar_t* wchars, unsigned ylen, unsigned xlen, unsigned ctlword) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1, 6)));
functions.description: Draws a box with its upper-left corner at the current cursor position using the provided corner channels (ul, ur, ll, lr) and wide-character set wchars = {UL, UR, LL, LR, HL, VL}. Dimensions are ylen by xlen. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
wchars must point to an array of at least 6 wide characters: UL, UR, LL, LR, HL, VL (not NULL).
Minimum box size is 2x2.
The box cannot be drawn off-screen.
Drawing starts at the current cursor position.

functions.name: ncdirect_rounded_box
functions.signature: API int ncdirect_rounded_box(struct ncdirect* n, uint64_t ul, uint64_t ur, uint64_t ll, uint64_t lr, unsigned ylen, unsigned xlen, unsigned ctlword) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1)));
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for ncdirect_box() using rounded box-drawing characters. Draws a ylen by xlen box at the current cursor. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
Minimum box size is 2x2 and it cannot be drawn off-screen (inherited from ncdirect_box()).

functions.name: ncdirect_double_box
functions.signature: API int ncdirect_double_box(struct ncdirect* n, uint64_t ul, uint64_t ur, uint64_t ll, uint64_t lr, unsigned ylen, unsigned xlen, unsigned ctlword) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1)));
functions.description: Convenience wrapper for ncdirect_box() using double-line box-drawing characters. Draws a ylen by xlen box at the current cursor. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
Minimum box size is 2x2 and it cannot be drawn off-screen (inherited from ncdirect_box()).

functions.name: ncdirect_get
functions.signature: API uint32_t ncdirect_get(struct ncdirect* n, const struct timespec* absdl, ncinput* ni) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1)));
functions.description: Reads a single input event. If absdl is NULL, blocks indefinitely. If absdl points to a zero timespec, operates non-blocking. Otherwise uses absdl as an absolute CLOCK_MONOTONIC deadline. Returns a Unicode code point, a synthesized special key constant, 0 on timeout, or (uint32_t)-1 on error. If an event is processed, the return is the id field from that event. If ni is non-NULL, it is filled with event details.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
absdl may be NULL (block), a pointer to {0,0} for non-blocking, or an absolute CLOCK_MONOTONIC deadline.
ni may be NULL if event details are not needed.

functions.name: ncdirect_inputready_fd
functions.signature: API int ncdirect_inputready_fd(struct ncdirect* n) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1)));
functions.description: Returns a file descriptor suitable for poll() to detect readiness of input for ncdirect_get_nblock(). This FD is not guaranteed to be stdin’s FD.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
Caller should use this FD with poll()/select() and then call ncdirect_get_nblock() when it becomes readable.

functions.name: ncdirect_stop
functions.signature: API int ncdirect_stop(struct ncdirect* nc);
functions.description: Releases the ncdirect context and associated resources. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: nc must be a context previously returned by ncdirect_init() or ncdirect_core_init().
Must not be used after being stopped.

functions.name: ncdirect_render_image
functions.signature: API int ncdirect_render_image(struct ncdirect* n, const char* filename, ncalign_e align, ncblitter_e blitter, ncscale_e scale) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1, 2)));
functions.description: Loads and displays an image file using the specified blitter and scaling. Output may scroll vertically; it occupies from the current cursor column to the right. You can instead split render/raster via ncdirect_render_frame() and ncdirect_raster_frame(). Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
filename must refer to an existing image file (not NULL).
Requires that the build has image support (FFmpeg/OIIO) for loading images.

functions.name: ncdirect_render_frame
functions.signature: API ALLOC ncdirectv* ncdirect_render_frame(struct ncdirect* n, const char* filename, ncblitter_e blitter, ncscale_e scale, int maxy, int maxx) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1, 2)));
functions.description: Renders an image from filename into an intermediate direct-mode visual using the given blitter/scale, but does not write it to the terminal. If maxy/maxx > 0, they limit the render size in cell units; otherwise terminal geometry is used. Returns a heap-allocated ncdirectv* on success, or NULL on error. Use ncdirect_raster_frame() to display and free it.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
filename must be a valid path to an image (not NULL).
If provided, maxy and maxx are cell dimensions; values <= 0 mean use terminal geometry.
Caller must later pass the returned ncdirectv* to ncdirect_raster_frame() (or otherwise free via the API that consumes it).

functions.name: ncdirect_raster_frame
functions.signature: API int ncdirect_raster_frame(struct ncdirect* n, ncdirectv* ncdv, ncalign_e align) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1, 2)));
functions.description: Writes a previously rendered direct-mode frame (from ncdirect_render_frame() or ncdirectf_render()) to the terminal with the given alignment. Frees the frame on all paths. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
ncdv must be a frame returned by ncdirect_render_frame() or ncdirectf_render() (not NULL).
Do not use ncdv after calling this function; it is freed.

functions.name: ncdirectf_from_file
functions.signature: API ALLOC ncdirectf* ncdirectf_from_file(struct ncdirect* n, const char* filename) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1, 2)));
functions.description: Loads media from disk into an ncvisual-like object for later rendering or geometry queries. Returns a heap-allocated ncdirectf* on success, NULL on error. Must be destroyed with ncdirectf_free().
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
filename must be a valid path to a media file (not NULL).
Caller must free the returned object with ncdirectf_free().

functions.name: ncdirectf_free
functions.signature: API void ncdirectf_free(ncdirectf* frame);
functions.description: Frees a ncdirectf object previously returned by ncdirectf_from_file(). Safe to call with NULL (unknown, but typical for free-like functions; unspecified here).
requirements: frame must be a pointer previously obtained from ncdirectf_from_file(); after return, it must not be used.

functions.name: ncdirectf_render
functions.signature: API ALLOC ncdirectv* ncdirectf_render(struct ncdirect* n, ncdirectf* frame, const struct ncvisual_options* vopts) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1, 2)));
functions.description: Renders a previously loaded frame (from ncdirectf_from_file()) according to vopts into an intermediate direct-mode visual without writing it. Returns a heap-allocated ncdirectv* on success, NULL on error. Display it with ncdirect_raster_frame().
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
frame must be a valid ncdirectf loaded by ncdirectf_from_file() (not NULL).
vopts may be NULL or point to options controlling render; exact fields are defined in ncvisual_options.

functions.name: ncdirectf_geom
functions.signature: API int ncdirectf_geom(struct ncdirect* n, ncdirectf* frame, const struct ncvisual_options* vopts, ncvgeom* geom) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1, 2)));
functions.description: Computes the geometry of a potential render of a loaded frame given options vopts, storing results in geom. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
frame must be a valid ncdirectf loaded by ncdirectf_from_file() (not NULL).
vopts may be NULL or a valid pointer to options.
geom may be NULL or a valid pointer to receive geometry; if non-NULL, it must point to writable storage.

functions.name: ncdirect_stream
functions.signature: API int ncdirect_stream(struct ncdirect* n, const char* filename, ncstreamcb streamer, struct ncvisual_options* vopts, void* curry) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1, 2)));
functions.description: Streams successive frames from a media file, invoking the callback streamer on each frame with optional vopts and user data curry. Returns 0 on success, non-zero on failure.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
filename must be a valid media path (not NULL).
streamer must be a valid callback function pointer; its calling convention is defined by ncstreamcb.
vopts may be NULL or a valid options pointer.
curry is user data passed to the callback; may be NULL.

functions.name: ncdirect_detected_terminal
functions.signature: ALLOC API char* ncdirect_detected_terminal(const struct ncdirect* n) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1)));
functions.description: Returns a heap-allocated string describing the detected terminal for this ncdirect context. Caller must free the returned string.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).
Caller must free the returned string.

functions.name: ncdirect_canutf8
functions.signature: API bool ncdirect_canutf8(const struct ncdirect* n) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1)));
functions.description: Returns whether the current encoding is UTF-8, typically requiring LANG to be set to a UTF-8 locale.
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).

functions.name: ncdirect_check_pixel_support
functions.signature: API int ncdirect_check_pixel_support(const struct ncdirect* n) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1)));
functions.description: Indicates whether pixel-accurate bitmap blitting is supported by the terminal. Returns an integer status (exact semantics defined by Notcurses).
requirements: n must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).

functions.name: ncdirect_canget_cursor
functions.signature: API bool ncdirect_canget_cursor(const struct ncdirect* nc) __attribute__ ((nonnull (1)));
functions.description: Returns whether the environment supports acquiring the cursor’s position (requires u7 terminfo capability and a real terminal).
requirements: nc must be a valid ncdirect context (not NULL).

functions.name: nckey_synthesized_p
functions.signature: static inline bool nckey_synthesized_p(uint32_t w)
functions.description: Returns true if w is a Notcurses-synthesized input event (keyboard, mouse, signal, window events) encoded beyond Unicode, i.e., in the inclusive range [PRETERUNICODEBASE, NCKEY_EOF]. Intended to distinguish internal/special key events from ordinary Unicode codepoints.
requirements: Argument w may be any uint32_t; no specific preconditions or state are required.
The function performs a pure range check and has no side effects; callers need not perform any cleanup.

functions.name: nckey_pua_p
functions.signature: static inline bool nckey_pua_p(uint32_t w)
functions.description: Returns true if w lies in the Unicode Basic Multilingual Plane Private Use Area (PUA), i.e., 0xE000 through 0xF8FF inclusive. Useful to detect application-defined codepoints within the BMP.
requirements: Argument w may be any uint32_t; no specific preconditions or state are required.
The function is a pure range check; callers need not handle errors.

functions.name: nckey_supppuaa_p
functions.signature: static inline bool nckey_supppuaa_p(uint32_t w)
functions.description: Returns true if w lies in the Supplementary Private Use Area-A (SPUA-A), i.e., 0xF0000 through 0xFFFFD inclusive. Useful for identifying application-defined codepoints in SPUA-A.
requirements: Argument w may be any uint32_t; no specific preconditions or state are required.
Pure range check; no side effects or error handling required.

functions.name: nckey_supppuab_p
functions.signature: static inline bool nckey_supppuab_p(uint32_t w)
functions.description: Returns true if w lies in the Supplementary Private Use Area-B (SPUA-B), i.e., 0x100000 through 0x10FFFD inclusive. Useful for identifying application-defined codepoints in SPUA-B.
requirements: Argument w may be any uint32_t; no specific preconditions or state are required.
Pure range check; no side effects or error handling required.

functions.name: ncpp::NotCurses::NotCurses
functions.signature: explicit ncpp::NotCurses::NotCurses(FILE *fp = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructs a NotCurses instance using default_notcurses_options and an optional FILE* for logging/debug output. Initializes the underlying notcurses context.
requirements: Must not be copied or moved; copy/move constructors are deleted.
If a FILE* is supplied, it must be a valid, open FILE pointer for the lifetime of construction.
Only one active NotCurses instance should exist at a time for a given process/TTY context (implied by singleton-like get_instance and destructor closing notcurses).
Creation may throw if initialization fails (inferred from typical RAII patterns; details unknown).

functions.name: ncpp::NotCurses::~NotCurses
functions.signature: ncpp::NotCurses::~NotCurses()
functions.description: Destructor for NotCurses. Shuts down and releases the underlying notcurses context and any associated resources.
requirements: Must ensure no operations are performed on this instance after destruction.
Destroying a NotCurses instance likely affects global state for the process’s notcurses session; other references to the same context become invalid (implied by comments).

functions.name: ncpp::NotCurses::operator notcurses*
functions.signature: ncpp::NotCurses::operator notcurses* () noexcept
functions.description: Implicit conversion operator to obtain the underlying mutable notcurses* handle.
requirements: The returned pointer may be null if the instance has been stopped or not initialized; callers must check for null before use.

functions.name: ncpp::NotCurses::operator notcurses const*
functions.signature: ncpp::NotCurses::operator notcurses const* () const noexcept
functions.description: Implicit conversion operator to obtain the underlying const notcurses* handle.
requirements: The returned pointer may be null if the instance has been stopped or not initialized; callers must check for null before use.

functions.name: ncpp::NotCurses::get_instance
functions.signature: static ncpp::NotCurses& ncpp::NotCurses::get_instance()
functions.description: Returns the current NotCurses singleton-like instance. Throws if no instance exists or if its internal notcurses pointer is null.
requirements: A NotCurses instance must have been successfully constructed before calling.
May throw invalid_state_error if no instance is present or if internal state is invalid.

functions.name: ncpp::NotCurses::is_notcurses_stopped
functions.signature: static bool ncpp::NotCurses::is_notcurses_stopped(const NotCurses *ncinst = nullptr)
functions.description: Checks whether notcurses has been stopped for the provided instance or, if none provided, for the global instance.
requirements: If ncinst is provided, it must be either a valid NotCurses pointer or null; when provided, the function checks ncinst->nc == nullptr.
If no instance has been created and ncinst is null, the function treats it as stopped (returns true).

functions.name: ncpp::NotCurses::ncmetric
functions.signature: static const char* ncpp::NotCurses::ncmetric(uintmax_t val, uintmax_t decimal, char *buf, int omitdec, unsigned mult, int uprefix) noexcept
functions.description: Formats a numeric value into a human-readable metric string with the specified multiplier and unit prefixing strategy. Thin wrapper around ncnmetric.
requirements: buf must point to a writable character buffer large enough to hold the formatted result (exact size requirements unknown; library-defined).
Parameters decimal, omitdec, mult, and uprefix must be within acceptable ranges for ncnmetric (exact constraints unknown).

functions.name: ncpp::NotCurses::ncqprefix
functions.signature: static const char* ncpp::NotCurses::ncqprefix(uintmax_t val, uintmax_t decimal, char *buf, int omitdec) noexcept
functions.description: Formats a numeric value with a binary (power-of-two) quantity prefix into the provided buffer. Wrapper around ncqprefix.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer large enough for the formatted text (exact size unknown).

functions.name: ncpp::NotCurses::nciprefix
functions.signature: static const char* ncpp::NotCurses::nciprefix(uintmax_t val, uintmax_t decimal, char *buf, int omitdec) noexcept
functions.description: Formats a numeric value with an SI (decimal) prefix into the provided buffer. Wrapper around nciprefix.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer large enough for the formatted text (exact size unknown).

functions.name: ncpp::NotCurses::ncbprefix
functions.signature: static const char* ncpp::NotCurses::ncbprefix(uintmax_t val, uintmax_t decimal, char *buf, int omitdec) noexcept
functions.description: Formats a numeric value with a binary (IEC) prefix into the provided buffer. Wrapper around ncbprefix.
requirements: buf must point to a writable buffer large enough for the formatted text (exact size unknown).

functions.name: ncpp::NotCurses::str_blitter

functions.name: ncpp::NotCurses::str_scalemode

functions.description: Returns a human-readable name for a given scaling mode enumeration value.

scalemode must be a valid writable pointer.

functions.name: ncpp::FDPlane::FDPlane
functions.signature: ncpp::FDPlane::FDPlane(ncpp::Plane* plane, int fd, ncfdplane_callback cbfxn = nullptr, ncfdplane_done_cb donecbfxn = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructs an FDPlane widget bound to an existing ncpp::Plane using a file descriptor as input to an underlying ncfdplane. This overload forwards to the options-taking constructor with opts = nullptr, causing FDPlane::default_options to be used. Callbacks can be supplied to receive ncfdplane events and completion notification.
requirements: plane must be a valid, initialized ncpp::Plane instance; if passed as a pointer, it must be non-null.
fd must be a valid operating system file descriptor appropriate for use by notcurses ncfdplane (e.g., open and usable).
If cbfxn is non-null, it must be a valid function pointer conforming to ncfdplane_callback.
If donecbfxn is non-null, it must be a valid function pointer conforming to ncfdplane_done_cb.
On success, the FDPlane takes ownership of the provided Plane; callers must not destroy or otherwise manage the Plane independently after construction.
Construction may throw init_error if ncfdplane_create fails; callers must be prepared to handle this exception.
This constructor must be called when Notcurses is running; constructing after Notcurses shutdown may fail.

functions.name: ncpp::FDPlane::~FDPlane
functions.signature: ncpp::FDPlane::~FDPlane()
functions.description: Destroys the FDPlane widget, releasing the underlying ncfdplane. If Notcurses has already been stopped, the destructor exits early without calling ncfdplane_destroy.
requirements: The FDPlane object must not be used after destruction.

If Notcurses is still running, the destructor will call ncfdplane_destroy on the managed ncfdplane handle; callers should ensure any external references to the underlying ncfdplane are no longer used.

functions.name: ncpp::FDPlane::get_plane

requirements: May only be called on a successfully constructed FDPlane instance.
The returned pointer refers to the plane owned by this FDPlane; callers must not delete it independently.
Function is noexcept; callers must not rely on exceptions for error handling here.

functions.name: ncpp::MultiSelector::MultiSelector
functions.signature: explicit ncpp::MultiSelector::MultiSelector(ncpp::Plane* plane, const ncmultiselector_options* opts = nullptr)

functions.name: ncpp::Palette::Palette
functions.signature: ncpp::Palette::Palette(ncpp::NotCurses* ncinst = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructs a Palette object and allocates an underlying ncpalette using the associated NotCurses instance (either the provided ncinst or that managed by the Root base). Throws init_error if palette allocation fails. Use this to manage a notcurses color palette in C++ code.
requirements: If ncinst is provided, it must point to a valid, initialized ncpp::NotCurses instance compatible with Root.
Callers must be prepared to handle exceptions (init_error) if allocation fails.
The resulting Palette owns the underlying ncpalette and will free it in the destructor.

functions.name: ncpp::Palette::~Palette
functions.signature: ncpp::Palette::~Palette()
functions.description: Destructor; releases the underlying ncpalette associated with this Palette. After destruction, any derived native pointer obtained earlier becomes invalid.
requirements: Do not use the Palette or any previously obtained native ncpalette pointer after the destructor runs.
Do not attempt to free the returned native ncpalette* yourself; it is freed here.

functions.name: ncpp::Palette::operator ncpalette*
functions.signature: ncpp::Palette::operator ncpalette*() noexcept
functions.description: Implicit conversion operator to the underlying mutable ncpalette*. Useful for passing this object directly to C notcurses APIs that take ncpalette*. The pointer is owned by this Palette and must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid only for the lifetime of the Palette instance.
Callers must not free or otherwise destroy the returned ncpalette*.
Behavior is undefined if used after the Palette is destroyed.

functions.name: ncpp::Palette::operator ncpalette const*
functions.signature: ncpp::Palette::operator ncpalette const*() const noexcept
functions.description: Implicit conversion operator to the underlying const ncpalette*. Useful for passing to C notcurses APIs requiring a const ncpalette*. The pointer is owned by this Palette and must not be freed by the caller.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid only for the lifetime of the Palette instance.
Callers must not free or otherwise destroy the returned ncpalette*.
Behavior is undefined if used after the Palette is destroyed.

functions.name: ncpp::Palette::set
functions.signature: bool ncpp::Palette::set(int idx, int r, int g, int b) const NOEXCEPT_MAYBE
functions.description: Sets the palette entry at index idx to the specified RGB components via the underlying ncpalette_set_rgb8. Intended to assign an 8-bit-per-channel color to a palette slot.
requirements: r, g, and b are 8-bit channel values (inferred from rgb8 naming), typically in the range 0–255.
idx must refer to a valid palette index supported by the underlying notcurses palette implementation (exact range is library-dependent and not specified here).
The return value must be checked: true indicates success; false indicates failure.

functions.name: ncpp::Palette::get
functions.signature: bool ncpp::Palette::get(int idx, unsigned* r, unsigned* g, unsigned* b) const
functions.description: Retrieves the RGB components of the palette entry at index idx into the provided pointers. Validates that output pointers are non-null and throws invalid_argument if any are null. Internally delegates to the reference overload backed by ncpalette_get_rgb8.
requirements: r, g, and b must be non-null pointers to writable unsigned variables; otherwise invalid_argument is thrown.
Callers must be prepared to handle exceptions (invalid_argument) for null pointers.
idx must refer to a valid palette index supported by the underlying notcurses palette implementation (exact range is library-dependent and not specified here).
On success, the pointed-to values receive 8-bit channel values (inferred from rgb8 naming), typically 0–255.
The return value must be checked: true indicates success; false indicates failure.

functions.name: ncpp::Pile::Pile
functions.signature: ncpp::Pile::Pile(const ncplane_options* nopts, NotCurses* ncinst = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructs a Pile (a top-level compositing group) around a newly created ncplane pile using the provided ncplane_options and a NotCurses context. If ncinst is nullptr, it attempts to use the global NotCurses instance. Throws if nopts is null or if the underlying notcurses pile creation fails. Typical usage: allocate a Pile to manage rendering/rasterization of a set of planes as a unit.
requirements: nopts must be a non-null pointer to a properly initialized ncplane_options structure.
If ncinst is provided, it must point to a valid NotCurses instance; if nullptr, a global NotCurses instance must be available (via NotCurses::get_instance).
May throw invalid_argument if nopts is null.
May throw init_error if the notcurses pile could not be created (ncpile_create returned nullptr).
The constructed object owns/wraps a valid ncplane representing the pile; subsequent member calls require successful construction.

functions.name: ncpp::Pile::render
functions.signature: bool ncpp::Pile::render() const NOEXCEPT_MAYBE
functions.description: Renders the pile associated with this Pile into the internal framebuffer (but does not write it to the terminal). Returns true on success, false on failure. Intended to be called before rasterize() or via show().
requirements: This Pile must have been constructed successfully and wrap a valid ncplane/pile.
Returns false if ncpile_render returns -1; otherwise true.
Does not display output to the terminal; use rasterize() to flush to the terminal.
Must not be called on a destroyed or invalid Pile instance.

functions.name: ncpp::Pile::rasterize
functions.signature: bool ncpp::Pile::rasterize() const NOEXCEPT_MAYBE
functions.description: Flushes the last rendered framebuffer of this Pile to the terminal (performs the rasterization/display step). Returns true on success, false on failure. Typically used after render(), or use show() to do both steps.
requirements: This Pile must have been constructed successfully and wrap a valid ncplane/pile.
Returns false if ncpile_rasterize returns -1; otherwise true.
A prior successful render() is recommended for meaningful output; show() performs both steps.
Must not be called on a destroyed or invalid Pile instance.

functions.name: ncpp::Pile::show
functions.signature: bool ncpp::Pile::show() const NOEXCEPT_MAYBE
functions.description: Convenience method that renders the pile and then rasterizes it to the terminal. Returns true only if both render() and rasterize() succeed.
requirements: This Pile must have been constructed successfully and wrap a valid ncplane/pile.
Returns false if render() fails or if rasterize() fails; otherwise true.
Equivalent to: if (!render()) return false; return rasterize();

functions.name: ncpp::Pile::top_with
functions.signature: static Plane* ncpp::Pile::top_with(const Plane& plane) noexcept
functions.description: Returns the topmost Plane within the same pile as the provided Plane. If no top plane can be determined or on failure, returns nullptr. Useful for querying the compositing order within a pile.
requirements: plane must reference a valid Plane that is currently associated with a pile.
Returns a mapped Plane* for the top ncplane in that pile, or nullptr on failure.
The returned Plane* is managed by the internal mapping (map_plane); do not assume ownership or attempt to delete it.

functions.name: ncpp::Pile::bottom_with
functions.signature: static Plane* ncpp::Pile::bottom_with(const Plane& plane) noexcept
functions.description: Returns the bottommost Plane within the same pile as the provided Plane. If no bottom plane can be determined or on failure, returns nullptr. Useful for querying the compositing order within a pile.
requirements: plane must reference a valid Plane that is currently associated with a pile.
Returns a mapped Plane* for the bottom ncplane in that pile, or nullptr on failure.
The returned Plane* is managed by the internal mapping (map_plane); do not assume ownership or attempt to delete it.

functions.name: ncpp::PlotBase<TPlot, TCoord>::add_sample
functions.signature:
template<typename TPlot, typename TCoord>
bool ncpp::PlotBase<TPlot, TCoord>::add_sample(uint64_t x, TCoord y) const NOEXCEPT_MAYBE
functions.description: Adds a sample to the underlying notcurses plot at domain coordinate x with value y. For PlotD (TCoord=double) this calls ncdplot_add_sample; for PlotU (TCoord=uint64_t) it calls nduplot_add_sample. Returns true on success and false on failure via an internal error guard. Typical use is to stream or append samples into the plot after construction.
requirements: This method must be called on a successfully constructed PlotBase (i.e., the underlying plot pointer is non-null).
Argument y must be of the same coordinate type used by the instance (double for PlotD or uint64_t for PlotU).
Callers should check the boolean return value and handle failure (false).
Behavior or requirements on monotonicity or range of x/y are unknown from this header.

functions.name: ncpp::PlotBase<TPlot, TCoord>::set_sample
functions.signature:
template<typename TPlot, typename TCoord>
bool ncpp::PlotBase<TPlot, TCoord>::set_sample(uint64_t x, TCoord y) const NOEXCEPT_MAYBE
functions.description: Sets or overwrites the sample at domain coordinate x to value y in the underlying plot. For double plots it calls ncdplot_set_sample; for uint64_t plots it calls nduplot_set_sample. Returns true on success, false on failure.
requirements: This method must be called on a successfully constructed PlotBase instance.
Argument y must match the instance coordinate type (double for PlotD, uint64_t for PlotU).
Callers must check the boolean return value and handle failure.
Exact semantics of creating vs. updating a sample, and valid ranges for x/y, are unknown from this header.

functions.name: ncpp::PlotBase<TPlot, TCoord>::sample
functions.signature:
template<typename TPlot, typename TCoord>
bool ncpp::PlotBase<TPlot, TCoord>::sample(uint64_t x, TCoord* y) const NOEXCEPT_MAYBE
functions.description: Retrieves the sample value at domain coordinate x and stores it in *y. For double plots it calls ncdplot_sample; for uint64_t plots it calls ncuplot_sample. Returns true on success and false on failure.
requirements: This method must be called on a successfully constructed PlotBase instance.
Parameter y must be a valid, non-null pointer to storage for a TCoord result.
Callers must check the boolean return value and handle failure.
The existence requirements for a sample at x and the behavior when one is absent are unknown from this header.

functions.name: ncpp::PlotBase<TPlot, TCoord>::get_plot
functions.signature:
template<typename TPlot, typename TCoord>
TPlot* ncpp::PlotBase<TPlot, TCoord>::get_plot() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns the underlying notcurses plot handle (ncdplot* for double or ncuplot* for uint64_t). Useful for advanced operations directly against the C API.
requirements: The returned pointer is only valid for the lifetime of the PlotBase-derived object.
Do not use the returned pointer after the owning object is destroyed.
Any direct use must follow the notcurses C API’s requirements for the returned plot type.

functions.name: ncpp::PlotU::PlotU
functions.signature: explicit ncpp::PlotU::PlotU(Plane* plane, const ncplot_options* opts = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructs an unsigned-integer plot (ncuplot) on the given Plane. If opts is null, PlotU::default_options are used. Internally creates the underlying ncuplot and takes ownership of the Plane for widget use.
requirements: plane must refer to a valid Plane not already in use by another widget (the base class enforces plane->is_valid(), throwing invalid_argument otherwise).
A notcurses context associated with plane must be active so that plot creation can succeed; otherwise an init_error is thrown.
If opts is provided, it must be a valid pointer; passing nullptr is allowed and will use PlotU::default_options.
Construction throws on failure; callers must be prepared to handle exceptions invalid_argument and init_error.

functions.name: ncpp::PlotU::get_plane
functions.signature: Plane* ncpp::PlotU::get_plane() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns the Plane associated with this PlotU widget. Useful for accessing or manipulating the plane after construction.
requirements: The returned Plane* is valid only while the PlotU object (and its underlying notcurses resources) remain alive.
Do not use the returned pointer after the widget is destroyed.

functions.name: ncpp::PlotD::PlotD
functions.signature: explicit ncpp::PlotD::PlotD(Plane* plane, const ncplot_options* opts = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructs a double-precision plot (ncdplot) on the given Plane. If opts is null, PlotD::default_options are used. Internally creates the underlying ncdplot and takes ownership of the Plane.
requirements: plane must refer to a valid Plane not already in use by another widget; invalid planes cause invalid_argument to be thrown.
An active notcurses context is required; failures in creating the plot throw init_error.
If opts is provided, it must be a valid pointer; passing nullptr uses PlotD::default_options.
Construction throws on failure; callers must handle exceptions.

functions.name: ncpp::PlotD::get_plane
functions.signature: Plane* ncpp::PlotD::get_plane() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns the Plane associated with this PlotD widget.
requirements: The returned Plane* is valid only while the PlotD object remains alive.
Do not use the returned pointer after the widget is destroyed.

functions.name: ncpp::Progbar::Progbar
functions.signature: ncpp::Progbar::Progbar(Plane& n, const ncprogbar_options* opts)
functions.description: Constructs a progress bar widget on the given Plane using the provided ncprogbar_options. Throws invalid_argument if opts is null. Internally calls ncprogbar_create and throws init_error if creation fails. Use this to create and attach a Notcurses progress bar to an existing Plane.
requirements: opts must be a valid, non-null pointer (explicitly enforced; otherwise invalid_argument is thrown).
n must reference a valid, initialized ncpp::Plane associated with an active Notcurses context (inferred from usage of ncprogbar_create).
Caller must be prepared to handle exceptions: invalid_argument when opts is null; init_error if ncprogbar_create fails.
Should be called while Notcurses is initialized/running so that ncprogbar_create can succeed (inferred).

functions.name: ncpp::Progbar::~Progbar
functions.signature: ncpp::Progbar::~Progbar()
functions.description: Destroys the progress bar. If Notcurses is still running, releases the underlying ncprogbar via ncprogbar_destroy; if Notcurses has already been stopped, destruction of the underlying object is skipped. Typical RAII cleanup; no exceptions are thrown here.
requirements: Object must not be used after destruction.
No special caller action required; safe to destroy even after Notcurses shutdown since the destructor guards against destroying after stop (behavior inferred from is_notcurses_stopped check).

functions.name: ncpp::Progbar::get_plane
functions.signature: Plane* ncpp::Progbar::get_plane() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns the Plane associated with this progress bar, or nullptr if no plane is available. Wraps ncprogbar_plane and maps the returned ncplane to an ncpp::Plane if present. Intended for accessing or manipulating the underlying Plane of the progress bar.
requirements: The Progbar instance must be valid/initialized.
Caller must handle a possible nullptr return value before dereferencing the result.

functions.name: ncpp::Progbar::set_progress
functions.signature: void ncpp::Progbar::set_progress(double p) const noexcept
functions.description: Sets the current progress value of the progress bar to p. For typical progress bars, p is a fractional value from 0.0 to 1.0. This forwards to ncprogbar_set_progress and does not throw.
requirements: The Progbar instance must be valid/initialized.
p should be within the normalized range [0.0, 1.0] for meaningful behavior (inferred from progress bar semantics and ncprogbar naming).

functions.name: ncpp::Progbar::get_progress
functions.signature: double ncpp::Progbar::get_progress() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns the current progress value of the progress bar as reported by ncprogbar_progress. Typically a normalized fraction between 0.0 and 1.0.
requirements: The Progbar instance must be valid/initialized.
Returned value is typically within [0.0, 1.0] (inferred from progress bar semantics).

functions.name: ncpp::Reader::Reader
functions.signature: explicit ncpp::Reader::Reader(Plane* plane, const ncreader_options* opts)
functions.description: Constructor that creates a notcurses reader widget bound to the given Plane. It validates the Plane, initializes an ncreader with the provided options, and takes ownership of the Plane. Use this to instantiate a Reader when you already have a Plane pointer.
requirements: plane must refer to a valid Plane (ensure_valid_plane is called internally)
On success, the Reader takes ownership of plane; the caller must not delete or otherwise manage the lifetime of plane afterwards
opts is passed directly to ncreader_create; acceptable values and defaults are determined by the notcurses API (unknown here)
Throws an exception if the underlying ncreader_create call fails (init_error)

functions.name: ncpp::Reader::~Reader
functions.signature: ncpp::Reader::~Reader()
functions.description: Destructor for the Reader widget. It destroys the underlying ncreader if notcurses is still running. Cleanup is skipped if notcurses has already been stopped.
requirements: No caller action required; destruction is automatic
If notcurses is already stopped, the underlying ncreader is not destroyed (safe shutdown path)

functions.name: ncpp::Reader::clear
functions.signature: bool ncpp::Reader::clear() const
functions.description: Clears the reader’s contents via ncreader_clear. Returns a boolean indicating the result; exact success/failure semantics depend on the wrapped API and error_guard handling (details not visible here).
requirements: The Reader instance must have been successfully constructed
No arguments; can be called at any time after construction
Return value semantics are not specified in this header; callers should not assume true/false mapping without consulting the underlying API (unknown)

functions.name: ncpp::Reader::move_up

functions.description: Attempts to move the reader’s cursor one position up. Return value is informational: 0 when moved and -1 when not moved; not an error condition.
requirements: Reader must be valid and initialized
Return values are informational per comment: 0 means moved; -1 means not moved (per header comment)
Function is noexcept; callers should not expect exceptions

functions.name: ncpp::Reader::move_down

functions.description: Attempts to move the reader’s cursor one position down. Return value is informational: 0 when moved and -1 when not moved; not an error condition.

functions.name: ncpp::Reader::write_egc
functions.signature: bool ncpp::Reader::write_egc(const char* egc) const
functions.description: Writes a single extended grapheme cluster (EGC) to the reader via ncreader_write_egc. Returns a boolean indicating success/failure as mediated by error_guard; exact mapping is not specified here.

Reader must be valid and initialized
On error, the underlying API likely signals failure; exceptions may be thrown by error_guard (unknown exact behavior)

functions.name: ncpp::Reader::get_contents
functions.signature: char* ncpp::Reader::get_contents() const noexcept
functions.description: Retrieves the current contents of the reader as a C string via ncreader_contents. Ownership and lifetime of the returned buffer are not specified here.
requirements: Reader must be valid and initialized
Returned pointer may be null on failure (unknown); callers must handle null safely
Memory ownership, allocation method, and required deallocation (if any) are unknown from this header; callers must consult the notcurses API to determine whether and how to free the memory

functions.name: ncpp::Reader::get_plane
functions.signature: Plane* ncpp::Reader::get_plane() const noexcept
functions.description: Returns the Plane associated with this Reader by mapping the underlying ncplane from ncreader_plane to a C++ Plane. The Plane is managed by the Reader; callers should not free or delete it.

functions.name: ncpp::NcReel::NcReel
functions.signature: ncpp::NcReel::NcReel(ncpp::Plane& plane, const ncreel_options* popts = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructs an NcReel widget on the given Plane, creating the underlying ncreel with the provided options (or default_options if popts is null) and taking ownership of the Plane. Intended to host a scrollable set of tablets within the Plane.
requirements: plane must refer to a valid, initialized ncpp::Plane (validated via ensure_valid_plane).
On success, NcReel takes ownership of the Plane; callers must not destroy or otherwise manage the Plane independently after construction.
popts may be null to use NcReel::default_options; otherwise it must point to a valid ncreel_options structure.
Throws on failure to create the underlying ncreel (init_error).

functions.name: ncpp::NcReel::~NcReel
functions.signature: ncpp::NcReel::~NcReel()
functions.description: Destroys the NcReel, releasing the underlying ncreel unless notcurses has already been stopped. Called automatically when the object goes out of scope.
requirements: Object must have been successfully constructed prior to destruction.
Should not be called after the associated notcurses context is fully stopped; the implementation skips ncreel_destroy if notcurses is stopped.

functions.name: ncpp::NcReel::operator ncreel*
functions.signature: operator ncreel*() const noexcept
functions.description: Implicit conversion to the underlying ncreel* handle for interoperability with the C notcurses API.

functions.name: ncpp::NcReel::operator ncreel const*
functions.signature: operator ncreel const*() const noexcept
functions.description: Implicit conversion to the underlying ncreel const* handle for read-only interoperability with the C notcurses API.
requirements: The NcReel instance must be valid (constructed) when the conversion is used.
The returned pointer remains owned by NcReel; do not free or destroy it.

functions.name: ncpp::NcReel::add
functions.signature: ncpp::NcReel::NcTablet* add(ncpp::NcTablet* after, ncpp::NcTablet* before, tabletcb cb, void* opaque = nullptr) const
functions.description: Adds a new tablet to the reel, positioned relative to the provided 'after' and/or 'before' tablets, using the supplied callback to render the tablet content. Returns the newly created NcTablet wrapper. Throws if creation fails.

opaque is an optional user pointer passed to the callback and may be null.

functions.name: ncpp::NcReel::get_tabletcount

functions.description: Returns the number of tablets currently attached to the reel.

functions.name: ncpp::NcReel::del

functions.description: Removes the specified tablet from the reel. Returns true on success and false on error as mediated by error_guard.

functions.name: ncpp::NcReel::redraw

functions.description: Forces the reel to be redrawn by invoking the underlying ncreel_redraw. Returns true on success and false on failure as mediated by error_guard.

functions.name: ncpp::NcReel::get_focused

functions.name: ncpp::NcReel::prev

functions.name: ncpp::NcReel::offer_input

functions.name: ncpp::NcReel::get_plane

functions.name: ncpp::Root::get_notcurses

functions.name: ncpp::Root::get_notcurses_cpp

functions.name: ncpp::Root::is_notcurses_stopped

requirements: Intended to be called before invoking notcurses operations from destructors of objects that manage notcurses entities, to avoid segfaults after NotCurses::stop.
Noexcept: callers must not expect exceptions from this function.

functions.name: ncpp::Selector::Selector
functions.signature: ncpp::Selector::Selector(ncpp::Plane* plane, const ncselector_options* opts = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructs a Selector widget on the given Plane*, creating an underlying notcurses ncselector using the provided options or default_options if opts is null. Validates the plane and transfers plane ownership to the widget. Throws on invalid input or failed initialization.

functions.name: ncpp::Selector::~Selector
functions.signature: ncpp::Selector::~Selector()

requirements: The Selector must not be used after destruction
Relies on is_notcurses_stopped to avoid destroying after notcurses shutdown; callers should ensure standard lifetime ordering of widgets relative to notcurses shutdown

functions.name: ncpp::Selector::additem

functions.name: ncpp::Subproc::Subproc
functions.signature: explicit ncpp::Subproc::Subproc(Plane* plane, const char* bin, bool use_path = true, char* const arg[] = nullptr, char* const env[] = nullptr, ncfdplane_callback cbfxn = nullptr, ncfdplane_done_cb donecbfxn = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructs a Subproc widget on the given Plane*, launching the specified binary as a Notcurses subprocess and wiring it to an fdplane. This overload searches PATH when use_path is true and accepts optional argv/envp arrays and lifecycle callbacks. Internally delegates to the opts overload with default options, validates the plane and bin, creates the ncsubproc via notcurses (createv/createvp/createvpe), and takes ownership of the Plane.
requirements: plane must be a valid, initialized Plane pointer; it must not be null (validated via ensure_valid_plane).
bin must be a non-null C string; passing nullptr throws invalid_argument.
If use_path is false, bin should be an explicit executable path (inferred from createv vs createvp naming).
arg and env are argv/envp-style arrays of C strings, typically null-terminated (inferred from *v/*vpe naming).
cbfxn and donecbfxn, if provided, must match the ncfdplane_callback and ncfdplane_done_cb signatures expected by Notcurses.
On creation failure, the constructor throws init_error.
The Subproc takes ownership of the provided Plane; callers must not independently destroy or reassign that Plane after construction.

functions.name: ncpp::Subproc::~Subproc
functions.signature: ncpp::Subproc::~Subproc()
functions.description: Destroys the Subproc, releasing the underlying ncsubproc. If Notcurses has already been stopped, the destructor returns early; otherwise, it calls ncsubproc_destroy on the managed handle.
requirements: Must not rely on callbacks being invoked during destruction; destructor may be a no-op if Notcurses is already stopped.
Object should be destroyed before Notcurses shutdown to ensure ncsubproc_destroy is called; otherwise cleanup is skipped.

requirements: May return a non-owning Plane* managed by Subproc; callers must not delete it.
Function is noexcept; callers must not expect exceptions.
